text:
Alice Rivera: Quick copy review  Confirm modal for enabling Auto-batching. Current title: 'Enable Auto-batching?' Body: 'Auto-batching will group requests to reduce cost but may slightly increase latency. Enable now?' CTA primary: 'Enable', secondary: 'Cancel'. Tone feels terse. Thoughts?
Ben Cho: We should state benefit first. Suggest title: 'Enable Auto-batching to save on tokens' or shorter: 'Turn on Auto-batching?'. Body: 'Groups similar requests to lower per-token cost. May add small latency under peak load.'
Maya Singh: Dev constraints: we have 80 char limit in modal title, 210 in body. Also need to include a learn-more link to docs. Example link text should be 'How it works'.
Priya Iyer: Accessibility: modal should focus the primary CTA. For copy, avoid vague words like 'small'. Prefer 'up to ~X% latency' if we can supply a number, otherwise 'may increase latency slightly'. Also add aria-describedby for the learn-more link if it opens a new window: 'Opens in new tab'.
Leo Martinez: Marketing prefers benefit-forward language. Proposed primary CTA: 'Turn on Auto-batching' vs 'Enable'. Longer CTA better for accessibility but may truncate on mobile. We can have visible short CTA + aria-label full sentence.
Alice Rivera: Draft variants:
- Short title: 'Turn on Auto-batching?'
  Body: 'Group similar requests to lower per-token cost. May slightly increase latency under peak load.'
  CTA primary: 'Turn on Auto-batching' (aria-label: 'Turn on Auto-batching, opens settings')
  CTA secondary: 'Not now'
- Benefit-forward title: 'Save on tokens with Auto-batching'
  Body: 'Auto-batching groups compatible requests which can reduce cost by up to 30% on some workloads. Learn more.'
  CTA primary: 'Try Auto-batching' CTA secondary: 'Keep current settings'
Which to A/B?
Ben Cho: A/B short vs benefit-forward. Also test CTA phrasing: 'Turn on' vs 'Try' (less committal).
Maya Singh: Implementation note: include i18n keys and pluralization. Use `auto_batching.cta.primary.visible` and `auto_batching.cta.primary.aria` for explicit labels. For mobile truncation, fallback CTA to 'Enable'.
Priya Iyer: For screen readers, provide full context: aria-describedby should include "This will not delete data. Changes apply immediately." if that's true. If rollout is opt-in and reversible, say 'You can turn it off anytime.'
Leo Martinez: Approve benefit-forward copy. Also request a microcopy card with exact % placeholders: 'reduce cost by up to {{percent}}%' so localization can handle number formats.
copy-bot: Saved strings to copyboard. Keys: auto_batching.modal.title.short, auto_batching.modal.title.benefit, auto_batching.modal.body.short, auto_batching.modal.body.benefit, auto_batching.modal.cta.primary, auto_batching.modal.cta.secondary.
Alice Rivera: Action: I'll add both variants to the PR, Maya will wire i18n keys and mobile fallback, Priya will add aria-describedby snippets, Leo to sign off on final percentages. Thanks!
